newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament deadlocked on crisis deal.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament deadlocked on crisis deal.

text.p: Parliament in Belarus was deadlocked late on Friday over approving a compromise deal brokered by Russia aimed at ending its row with President Alexander Lukashenko.

Lukashenko returned to the chamber at 8.45 p.m. (1845 GMT) after parliamentary speaker Semyon Sharetsky invited him to try to solve the differences between pro- and anti-presidential groups in the chamber.
The move followed hours of debates and three failures to approve the agreement, hailed in Moscow as a major breakthrough but condemned by some deputies as a sellout to the president.
Deputies were split over whether the deal should be approved by a simple majority of the 199 members or a "constitutional" majority of two-thirds -- as Lukashenko wanted.
Lukashenko earlier set a deadline of 6 p.m. (1600 GMT) for deputies to approve the deal, under which he agreed that a referendum on Sunday on widening his powers would only be advisory.

Opposition deputies are worried Lukashenko will press ahead with plans to extend his powers and tighten his grip on rival institutions, since he will dominate a new constitutional commission envisaged under the deal.
